79487.subject: 🧥 Huang says the doomers are bluffing
79487.body:
The Atlas

Автор: GenAI Works


Автор: GenAI Works

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/huang-says-doomers-bluffing-genai-works-2hqxf?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3B9YvPwo9SR4Gx8J862A0g0Q%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=0Tw-RIFOuMecs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mubdb5io~wc-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mubdb5io-wc
  
Welcome back! Jensen Huang accused the safety crowd of asking for the opposite of what they claim, Anthropic built a lab where Claude runs the robots, and OpenAI published six things its models got caught doing.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: Huang says the safety crowd is asking for something else: What does he think they're really after? Anthropic puts more into biology: What costs $10,000 that Claude just did for $150? OpenAI published six things its models did wrong: What was the model hiding in its notes to itself? Cloudflare's vulnerability harness started as one skill: Why does the verifier's job start with trying to disprove the finding? PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Huang says the safety crowd is asking for something else Jensen Huang went on CBS on Sunday and accused frontier lab leaders of arguing in bad faith. His line: "Go and read between the lines. They're actually not asking for more laws. They're asking to be relieved of the laws we do have." Then: "They must be doing it for ulterior reasons." Asked what those reasons are, he said he didn't know, and called scaring people about the technology irresponsible and unnecessary. Worth checking his claim against the essay he's responding to.  Amodei's "We Must Pace the Frontier" proposes three things, and one of them asks the US government to regulate frontier labs specifically, on antitrust grounds.  Regulation aimed at the handful of companies at the top is a different request from regulation of the industry, which is roughly Huang's point. Altman amplified the essay. So did Musk. Huang's own position has not moved. A slowdown among US labs cedes ground to China, the labs can slow themselves down without asking Washington, and the rules already on the books just need enforcing. He now has company.  Trump posted Saturday that his administration will not hinder the growth of the industry. Michael Kratsios, who runs the White House science and technology office, told Fox on Sunday that labs worried about their products could simply stop. Two weeks ago Huang told a Goldman Sachs conference that alarm about AI security is good for the security business, asking what better way there is to create demand than to create a problem. He also sells the chips every side of this argument runs on. Master

79486.body:
AI Frontier

Автор: Steve Nouri


Автор: Steve Nouri

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення

https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/new-economics-ai-steve-nouri-yline?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3Bf8wRpTaDSeuPJKjG8jmPyQ%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3I60FhfRSCecs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mubdgmhb~gu-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mubdgmhb-gu
  
When Intelligence Gets Cheap, Where Does the Value Go? For the last few years, AI has been dominated by one question: Who has the best model? GPT vs Claude vs Gemini vs Qwen vs DeepSeek. Better reasoning. Bigger context windows. Lower prices. Better benchmarks. But I think we're approaching a much more interesting question: What happens when many models become good enough? Because when intelligence gets cheaper and more abundant, the value doesn't disappear. It moves. Get advice from 15+ enterprise leaders on operating intelligent agents Explore insights from leaders at global organizations on how to build adaptive agentic systems that create real business value in this Amazon Web Services (AWS) book. See their unique perspectives on how to shape agentic AI strategy, from architectural patterns and evaluation to comprehensive security and deployment. Learn how to: Build, monitor, and govern responsible AI agents at scale. Enhance agent performance and decision-making. Find the right AI architecture for your business needs. 👉 Get your digital copy 1. The model can be differentiated without being the moat Think about Coke and Pepsi. They aren't identical. The sweetness is different. The carbonation is different. The taste is different. But those differences don't fully explain why these companies became enormous. The real moat extends far beyond the formula: Brand. Distribution. Availability. Portfolio. Customer relationships. Habit. Trust. I think foundation models could follow a similar path. One model might be slightly better at coding. Another at reasoning. Another might be cheaper or faster. But if five models can successfully complete the same task, a small benchmark advantage may matter less than: Context → Data → Workflow → Distribution → Trust The model still matters. It just may not be where the entire moat lives. 2. When abundance arrives, scarcity moves There is a useful economic pattern here: When something valuable becomes abundant, value tends to move toward whatever remains scarce. We've seen this before. The internet made information abundant. Attention became scarce. GPS made location intelligence abundant. That helped unlock ride sharing, delivery, logistics and location-based services. Cloud computing made compute widely accessible. An enormous software economy was built on top of it. So what happens if AI makes intelligence abundant? I don't think intel

79481.subject: Is CARDS About to Rip?
79481.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

Gm everyone. As we begin the new week, I am excited to introduce you to our new newsletter format. We heard your feedback, and moving forward, we will be giving you daily unfiltered insights from our analysts into exactly what we are looking at. Let’s dive in.

If you have been following my work, you would know that I am a huge onchain collectibles bull, and the best proxy for that trade continues to be Collector Crypt. While BTC has pumped close to 30% from its $63K lows, CARDS has fallen 8% over the same period. So what has caused this, and is the collectibles trade over?

I view Collector Crypt’s current user base as Web 3 native memecoin and NFT degens looking for a quick dopamine hit. While these users can be big spenders on gacha machines, and they were, they are quick to move their capital when the next shiny object comes along. Most recently, that has been the memestock pairs going viral across Robinhood Chain and Solana.

This pulled capital away from the onchain collectibles space. You can see net revenue peak at $3M in the week ending August 16, just before launchpad volumes started taking off.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ea54ab24-0f40-4f9f-9821-bc8a2298e696/image.png?t=1789993787)
Caption: 

It really cannot be a coincidence that Collector Crypt’s metrics started falling just as launchpad volumes increased. But guess what? That is now starting to flip. Collector Crypt’s net revenue has bounced back after three weeks of decline and has put in two strong weeks as launchpad volumes have fallen.  

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/de552e9a-7a24-42a0-b61d-42794d17119a/image.png?t=1789993787)
Caption: 

Over the same period, the team has added new gacha machines to cater to the rising popularity of Riftbound and Dragon Ball packs. For those who have been to physical TCG conventions, you would know that these two TCGs have been heating up, almost like higher beta versions of the Pokémon and One Piece card price rally this year. I love how quickly the team has adapted to trends in the market, with these two categories accounting for 8% to 16% of gross revenue in recent weeks. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/35d4bdf8-9017-4d7c-b6e2-a36cf2914ccb/image.png?t=1789993787)
Caption:
